questions.question: The highest common factor of a set of coprime numbers is equal to:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Coprime numbers** (or relatively prime numbers) are defined as numbers that share no common factors other than **1**.

Since the only common factor is 1, the **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** must be 1.

Example: For the set {8, 9}, the factors of 8 are {1, 2, 4, 8} and the factors of 9 are {1, 3, 9}. The only common factor is 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** A set of **coprime numbers**.

**Definition:** Two or more numbers are **coprime** if their **greatest common divisor** is exactly 1.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/beb015cf070bd7d2d2dfc7988b7c1656b8aa9485cd88c08466ede00d6822b0be.png] 

⇒ Let the set of numbers be {x, y}.

⇒ Factors of x = {1, f₁, f₂, ...}

⇒ Factors of y = {1, g₁, g₂, ...}

⇒ If x and y are coprime, then {1, f₁, f₂, ...} ∩ {1, g₁, g₂, ...} = {1}.

⇒ The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is the largest value in the intersection set.

⇒ HCF = 1.

**∴ The correct answer is 1.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM of Coprime Numbers

The **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** of a set of coprime numbers is always equal to their **product** (e.g., LCM of 5 and 7 is 35).

Consecutive Numbers

Any two **consecutive natural numbers** (like 14 and 15) are always **coprime** to each other.

HCF and LCM Relationship

For any two numbers a and b, **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**. For coprime numbers, this simplifies to 1 × LCM = a × b.

Prime Numbers

Two different **prime numbers** are always coprime, but coprime numbers themselves do not necessarily have to be prime (e.g., 8 and 9 are coprime but composite).</p

questions.question: The HCF of the numbers 310, 208 and 180 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **HCF** of any set of numbers must divide the **difference** between any two of those numbers.

The difference between 208 and 180 is 28.

The factors of 28 are 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, and 28.

Since 310 is not divisible by 4, the HCF cannot be 4, 14, or 28.

Since all three numbers (310, 208, and 180) are **even numbers**, they are divisible by 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The numbers are 310, 208, and 180.

**Formula Used:**

**HCF** (Highest Common Factor) is the product of the **lowest powers** of all common prime factors.

**Calculations:**

Let us find the **prime factorisation** of each number:

⇒ 310 = 2 × 5 × 31

⇒ 208 = 2⁴ × 13

⇒ 180 = 2² × 3² × 5

Identify the common prime factors:

⇒ The only prime factor common to all three numbers is 2.

⇒ The lowest power of 2 among the factorisations is 2¹.

⇒ HCF = 2¹ = 2.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. It is also referred to as the **Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)**.

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The smallest non-zero common multiple of two or more numbers.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, the product of their HCF and LCM is equal to the product of the two numbers: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be **co-prime** if their HCF is 1.</p

questions.question: The LCM of 84, 105 and 140 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the **largest number** among 84, 105, and 140, which is 140.

Check the **multiples** of 140: 140, 280, 420...

Test 420: 420 ÷ 84 = 5 and 420 ÷ 105 = 4 and 420 ÷ 140 = 3.

Since 420 is the **least value** divisible by all three numbers, it is the **LCM**.

**∴ The correct answer is 420.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The numbers are 84, 105, and 140.

**Method:** **Prime Factorization** method involves expressing each number as a product of its prime factors.

⇒ 84 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7 = 2² × 3¹ × 7¹

⇒ 105 = 3 × 5 × 7 = 3¹ × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ 140 = 2 × 2 × 5 × 7 = 2² × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ To find the **LCM**, take the **highest power** of all prime factors (2, 3, 5, and 7) present in any of the numbers.

⇒ LCM = 2² × 3¹ × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ LCM = 4 × 3 × 5 × 7

⇒ LCM = 12 × 35 = 420

**∴ The correct answer is 420.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Least Common Multiple (LCM)

The **LCM** of two or more numbers is the smallest positive integer that is **perfectly divisible** by each of the given numbers.

Highest Common Factor (HCF)

The **HCF** is the greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. For 84, 105, and 140, the **HCF** is 7.

Product Rule

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b', the relationship is: **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**. Note that this rule does not directly apply to three or more numbers.</p

questions.question: The LCM of 24, 42, and 56 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Pick the **largest number** 56 and check its multiples for divisibility by 24 and 42.

Multiples of 56 are: 56, 112, 168, ...

Check 168: 168 ÷ 24 = 7 (Divisible) and 168 ÷ 42 = 4 (Divisible).

Since 168 is the first multiple of 56 divisible by both, it is the **LCM**.

**∴ The correct answer is 168.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 24, 42, and 56.

**Method:** Use the **Common Division Method** to find the **Least Common Multiple (LCM)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/551810143a71df8a1b24b44570c2d0797b8fc56ac13b7558e9858ddcc2b9f3fb.png] 

⇒ Prime factors obtained: 2, 2, 2, 3, 7

⇒ LCM = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 7

⇒ LCM = 8 × 21

⇒ LCM = 168

**∴ The correct answer is 168.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest positive integer that is **perfectly divisible** by each of the given numbers.

Relation between LCM and HCF

For two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their **HCF and LCM**: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Prime Factorization Method

LCM is the product of the **highest powers** of all prime factors present in any of the given numbers.</p

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is 84. If the numbers are in the ratio 2 : 3, then the sum of the numbers is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of numbers = 2 : 3

**LCM** of ratio parts (2 and 3) = 2 × 3 = 6 units

6 units = 84 ⇒ 1 unit = 14

Sum of numbers = (2 + 3) = 5 units

Sum = 5 × 14 = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

LCM of two numbers = 84

Ratio of the numbers = 2 : 3

**Formula Used:**

LCM of numbers ax and bx = (a × b) × x (where a and b are coprime)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0bc3ef8f466dd7dc5987dcd12a45c29ee84ea48a2b0b2e354da6fcedcdfecde9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the two numbers be 2x and 3x.

⇒ LCM of 2x and 3x = 6x

⇒ 6x = 84

⇒ x = 84 ÷ 6 = 14

⇒ Sum of the numbers = 2x + 3x = 5x

⇒ Sum = 5 × 14

⇒ Sum = 70

**∴ The correct answer is 70.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Relation of LCM and HCF

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM.

HCF and Ratio Relationship

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b and their HCF is x, then the numbers are ax and bx, and their LCM is a × b × x.

HCF of Coprime Numbers

The HCF of two coprime numbers is always 1, and their LCM is simply the product of the two numbers.</p

questions.question: If the HCF and the LCM of two numbers are 7 and 245, respectively, then their product is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **product of two numbers** is always equal to the product of their **HCF** and **LCM**.

Required Product = **HCF × LCM**

⇒ Product = 7 × 245 = 1715

**∴ The correct answer is 1715.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ **HCF** of two numbers = 7

⇒ **LCM** of two numbers = 245

**Formula used:**

⇒ **Number₁ × Number₂ = HCF × LCM**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1e38c8e480b28f6930615238d06d45ee327b28dd60604b8baa4e0a8e4489954f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Product of two numbers = 7 × 245

⇒ Product = 7 × (200 + 40 + 5)

⇒ Product = 1400 + 280 + 35

⇒ Product = 1715

**∴ The correct answer is 1715.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Property of HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers a and b, the relationship is **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**.

HCF as a Factor

The **HCF** of any set of numbers is always a **factor** of their **LCM**.

Co-prime Numbers

For **co-prime** numbers, the HCF is always **1** and the LCM is the **product** of the numbers themselves.</p

questions.question: The HCF of 450, 1500, and 1650 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The **HCF** of numbers is always equal to or a factor of the **difference** between any two of the numbers.

Difference between 1650 and 1500 = 1650 − 1500 = 150.

Check if 150 divides all numbers: 450 ÷ 150 = 3, 1500 ÷ 150 = 10, 1650 ÷ 150 = 11.

Since 150 divides all three numbers, it is the **Highest Common Factor**.

**∴ The correct answer is 150.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 450, 1500, and 1650.

**Method:** Prime Factorization method.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7d157241c7c5b425fbad6794aa948ff9751b21b40a079e956c0e37636d18a569.png] 

**Step-by-step Prime Factorization:**

⇒ 450 = 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 × 5 = 2¹ × 3² × 5²

⇒ 1500 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 × 5 × 5 = 2² × 3¹ × 5³

⇒ 1650 = 2 × 3 × 5 × 5 × 11 = 2¹ × 3¹ × 5² × 11¹

⇒ Common factors are 2¹, 3¹, and 5².

⇒ HCF = 2 × 3 × 25 = 150.

**∴ The correct answer is 150.**

**__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

The greatest number that divides two or more numbers without leaving a remainder. It is also known as **Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)**.

HCF Difference Property

The HCF of a set of numbers is always a factor of the difference between any two numbers in the set. If HCF(a, b) = k, then k also divides |a − b|.

Relationship between LCM and HCF

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b', the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Successive Division Method

To find the HCF of large numbers, divide the larger number by the smaller one, then divide the previous divisor by the remainder, until the remainder becomes zero.</p

questions.question: Two numbers are in the ratio 3 : 2. Their LCM and HCF are 24 and 4, respectively. The greater of the two numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the **ratio** of two numbers is **a : b** and their **HCF** is **H**, the numbers are **a × H** and **b × H**.

Given **Ratio** = 3 : 2 and **HCF** = 4.

Greater number = 3 × 4 = 12.

Smaller number = 2 × 4 = 8.

Verification: LCM of 12 and 8 is 24, which matches the given data.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Ratio = 3 : 2, **LCM** = 24, **HCF** = 4.

**Formula:** Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1ad0c6fb428db801fc3d2cf6112fe7990be3ef13c1c91ddc78de0df6ce0644f6.png] 

⇒ Let the two numbers be 3x and 2x.

⇒ The **HCF** of 3x and 2x is x (since 3 and 2 are co-prime).

⇒ Given **HCF** = 4, so x = 4.

⇒ Number 1 = 3x = 3 × 4 = 12.

⇒ Number 2 = 2x = 2 × 4 = 8.

⇒ Comparing the two numbers, 12 is greater than 8.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Property of HCF and LCM

For any two positive integers a and b: a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b).

Ratio and LCM Relationship

If two numbers are in the ratio x : y and their HCF is H, then their LCM = x × y × H.

Co-prime Numbers

Two numbers are said to be co-prime if their **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is 1.</p

questions.question: If LCM (27, n) = 54 and HCF (27, n) = 9, then the value of n is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **product of two numbers** is always equal to the product of their **LCM** and **HCF**.

First number × Second number = **LCM** × **HCF**

27 × **n** = 54 × 9

**n** = (54 × 9) ÷ 27 = 2 × 9 = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** First number = 27, **LCM(27, n)** = 54, **HCF(27, n)** = 9.

**Formula Used:** Product of two numbers = **LCM** × **HCF**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a88457e648797926f49308946ca30386f44d8b873033fb96431daab4c65d56f6.png] 

⇒ 27 × n = 54 × 9

⇒ 27n = 486

⇒ n = 486 ÷ 27

⇒ n = 18

**∴ The correct answer is 18.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Property of LCM and HCF

For any two positive integers a and b, the relationship is defined as: HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b.

Divisibility Rule

The **HCF** of any group of numbers is always a factor of their **LCM**. Here, 9 is a factor of 54.

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are **co-prime**, their **HCF** is 1, and their **LCM** is the product of the numbers themselves.</p

questions.question: Seven bells ring at intervals of 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 12 minutes, respectively. They started ringing simultaneously at 7.10 in the morning. What will be the next time when they all ring simultaneously?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **next simultaneous ring time** is always the **LCM** (Least Common Multiple) of the given time intervals.

Intervals: 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12 minutes.

**LCM** (2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12) = **72 minutes**.

72 minutes = 1 hour 12 minutes.

Next time = **7:10 a.m.** + 1 hour 12 minutes = **8:22 a.m.**

**∴ The correct answer is 8.22 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Intervals of 7 bells are **2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9 and 12 minutes**. Starting time is **7:10 a.m.**

**Formula Used:** Next simultaneous event = Start time + **LCM** of individual intervals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9a1cfd0da63822646c5d6051ad84a4721be100aca7344bb1625db2c29e584176.png] 

Calculating the **LCM** of 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12:

⇒ 2 = 2¹

⇒ 3 = 3¹

⇒ 4 = 2²

⇒ 6 = 2 × 3

⇒ 8 = 2³

⇒ 9 = 3²

⇒ 12 = 2² × 3

⇒ **LCM** = Highest powers of prime factors = 2³ × 3² = 8 × 9 = **72 minutes**.

Converting 72 minutes into hours:

⇒ 72 min = 60 min + 12 min = **1 hour 12 minutes**.

Adding the duration to the initial start time:

⇒ **7.10 a.m.** + 1 hour 12 minutes

⇒ 7 + 1 = 8 hours | 10 + 12 = 22 minutes

⇒ **8:22 a.m.**

**∴ The correct answer is 8.22 a.m.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

LCM (Least Common Multiple)

The smallest positive integer that is divisible by each of the numbers in a given set. It is widely used to find common meeting points in periodic events.

Ringing Bells & Circular Tracks

In problems involving bells, traffic lights, or runners on a circular track, the time when they all meet again is the **LCM** of their individual time periods.

Time Conversion

Always ensure the calculated duration is added carefully to the start time: **Total Minutes ÷ 60** gives the hours, and the **remainder** gives the additional minutes.</p

questions.solution:

Numbers = 105 and 120

HCF is calculated using the Euclidean algorithm:

If a > b, then HCF(a, b) = HCF(b, a mod b)

**Calculations:**

Step 1: Apply Euclidean Algorithm:

⇒ HCF(120, 105)

⇒ 120 mod 105 = 15

⇒ HCF(105, 15)

⇒ 105 mod 15 = 0

⇒ When remainder = 0, HCF = divisor

⇒ HCF = 15

**∴ The correct answer is option (2).**

questions.question: How many pairs of positive integers p, q exist such that the HCF of p, q is 37 and the sum of p and q is 1961?
questions.solution:
Given:

HCF(p, q) = 37

p + q = 1961

Calculation:

Let p = 37a, q = 37b where a and b are co-prime positive integers

⇒ p + q = 37a + 37b = 1961

⇒ 37(a + b) = 1961

⇒ a + b = 1961 / 37 = 53

Now, find number of positive integer pairs (a, b) such that:

⇒ a + b = 53 and HCF(a, b) = 1

Let a range from 1 to 26 (as b = 53 − a)

We count only those (a, b) such that HCF(a, 53 − a) = 1

Since 53 is a prime number, all pairs (a, 53 − a) with a = 1 to 26 are co-prime

⇒ Total such pairs = 26

∴ Required number of positive integer pairs (p, q) = __26__

questions.question: If the least common multiple of 85 and 255 can be expressed as 85R+255, then the value of R is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 85 and 255

Least Common Multiple (LCM) = 85R + 255

**Formula Used:**

LCM = (Product of numbers) / (Greatest Common Divisor (GCD))

**Calculation:**

⇒ LCM (85, 255) = 255

⇒ LCM = 85R + 255

Substitute LCM = 255 into the equation:

⇒ 255 = 85R + 255

⇒ 85R = 255 - 255

⇒ 85R = 0

⇒ R = 0

**The value of R is 0.**

40 = 2³ × 5

50 = 2 × 5²

78 = 2 × 3 × 13

Take the highest power of each prime factor:

2³, 3, 5², 13

LCM = 2³ × 3 × 5² × 13

⇒ LCM = 8 × 3 × 25 × 13

⇒ LCM = 7800

**The LCM of 12, 40, 50, and 78 is 7800.**

questions.solution:
**Given:**

questions.question: Two numbers X and Y are in ratio as 8 : 13. The LCM of these two numbers is 832. How much the value of Y is more than X?

 X 8 units Y 13 units

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let X = 8k and Y = 13k (where k is the common factor/HCF)

⇒ LCM(8k, 13k) = 8 × 13 × k = 104k

⇒ 104k = 832

⇒ k = 832 ÷ 104

⇒ k = 8

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two numbers A and B, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF × LCM.

Co-prime Numbers

Numbers that have only 1 as their common factor are called co-prime. The LCM of two co-prime numbers is simply their product.

questions.question: Four chimes ring simultaneously at 5:30 a.m. After that, they ring at the intervals of 15 seconds, 20 seconds, 25 seconds and 30 seconds, respectively. How many times will these chimes ring together till 8:15 a.m., including at 5:30 a.m.?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Four chimes ring simultaneously at 5:30 a.m.

Intervals of the chimes: 15 seconds, 20 seconds, 25 seconds, and 30 seconds.

Time duration: From 5:30 a.m. to 8:15 a.m.

**Formula used:**

To find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of the intervals, use:

LCM of (15, 20, 25, 30).

Then calculate the total time in seconds and divide it by the LCM to find the total number of times the chimes ring together.

**Calculation:**

LCM of 15, 20, 25, and 30:

Prime factorization:

15 = 3 × 5

20 = 2² × 5

25 = 5²

30 = 2 × 3 × 5

LCM = 2² × 3 × 5² = 300 seconds.

Total time from 5:30 a.m. to 8:15 a.m.:

2 hours 45 minutes = (2 × 3600) + (45 × 60) = 7200 + 2700 = 9900 seconds.

Number of times the chimes ring together:

⇒ Total time (in seconds) ÷ LCM + 1 (including initial time at 5:30 a.m.)

⇒ 9900 ÷ 300 + 1

⇒ 33 + 1 = 34.

**∴ The correct answer is option (3).**

Factors of 12: (1,12), (2,6), (3,4)

Co-prime pairs: (1,12), (3,4)

⇒ Total valid co-prime pairs = 2

**∴ The number of such pairs is 2.**

questions.question: The LCM of 2³ × 3² × 5 × 11, 2⁴ × 3⁴ × 5² × 7, and 2⁵ × 3³ × 5³ × 7² × 11 is _____.

To find the Least Common Multiple (LCM) of numbers expressed in their prime factorized form, we take the highest power of each prime factor that appears in any of the given numbers.

**Calculation:**

The highest power of 3 is 3⁴.

The highest power of 5 is 5³.

The highest power of 7 is 7².

The highest power of 11 is 11¹.

Combine these highest powers to get the LCM:

LCM = 2⁵ × 3⁴ × 5³ × 7² × 11

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: If the LCM of x × √y and y × √x is I, then the LCM of 4 × x³ × √y⁶ and y³ × √(4 × x⁶) is ______.

questions.question: Find the HCF of 84, 126 and 210.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Calculate the **differences** between consecutive numbers: 126 − 84 = **42** and 210 − 126 = **84**.

The **HCF** is either the **smallest difference** or a **factor** of that difference.

Smallest difference = 42.

Check if 42 divides all: 84 ÷ 42 = 2, 126 ÷ 42 = 3, and 210 ÷ 42 = 5.

Since 42 divides all given numbers, it is the **Highest Common Factor**.

**∴ The correct answer is 42.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers 84, 126, and 210.

**Formula Used:** **Prime Factorization Method** (HCF = Product of common prime factors with lowest powers).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3c8309477f30701f8351807f774fb322a6c0d12d131e39fbd790b5b6dc97747f.png] 

⇒ Prime factors of 84 = 2² × 3¹ × 7¹

⇒ Prime factors of 126 = 2¹ × 3² × 7¹

⇒ Prime factors of 210 = 2¹ × 3¹ × 5¹ × 7¹

⇒ HCF = 2¹ × 3¹ × 7¹

⇒ HCF = 2 × 3 × 7

⇒ HCF = 42

**∴ The correct answer is 42.**

**__Additional Information__**

Definition of HCF

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**, also known as the **Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)**, is the greatest number that divides all given numbers exactly.

HCF of Prime and Co-prime Numbers

The HCF of any two or more **prime numbers** or **co-prime numbers** is always **1**.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b, the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**.

HCF of Fractions

HCF of Fractions = (HCF of **Numerators**) ÷ (LCM of **Denominators**).</p

questions.question: Five bells toll together initially and then continue to toll at time intervals of 4, 8, 12, 16 and 20 seconds respectively. If they start tolling simultaneously at 12:00 p.m., then find how many times they will toll together between 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Five bells toll together initially and then continue to toll at time intervals of 4, 8, 12, 16, and 20 seconds respectively.

**Formula used:**

LCM of the time intervals will give the interval at which all the bells toll together.

**Calculation:**

LCM of (4, 8, 12, 16, 20)

Prime factorization:

4 = 2²

8 = 2³

12 = 2² × 3

16 = 2⁴

20 = 2² × 5

LCM = 2⁴ × 3 × 5 = 16 × 3 × 5 = 240 seconds

240 seconds = 4 minutes

From 12:00 p.m. to 3:00 p.m., there are 3 hours = 180 minutes

⇒ Total times they toll together = 180 / 4 + 1 (including the first toll at 12:00 p.m.)

⇒ Total times = 45 + 1 = 46

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: The LCM of two numbers is seven times of their HCF. If the product of two numbers is 448, then find the difference between LCM and HCF.

Product of numbers = 448

⇒ 7x × x = 448

⇒ 7x² = 448

⇒ x² = 64

⇒ x = 8

⇒ HCF = 8

⇒ LCM = 7 × 8 = 56

Difference between LCM and HCF = 56 - 8 = 48

**∴ The correct answer is option (4).**

questions.question: The ratio between HCF and LCM of two numbers 62 and 217 is 1 : 14. Find the LCM.

⇒ x² = 961

⇒ x = √961 = 31

**HCF = 31**

**LCM** = 14x = 14 × 31 = **434**

**∴ The LCM is 434.**

questions.question: The greatest common divisor (GCD) and least common multiple (LCM) of two numbers are 12 and 480, respectively, and the numbers are in the ratio of 5 : 8. Find the difference between the two numbers.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

GCD of two numbers = 12

LCM of two numbers = 480

The ratio of the two numbers = 5 : 8

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = GCD × LCM

Let the two numbers be 5x and 8x.

Product of two numbers = (5x) × (8x)

**Calculations**

GCD × LCM = (5x) × (8x)

→ 12 × 480 = 40x²

→ 5760 = 40x²

→ x² = 5760 / 40

→ x² = 144

→ x = √144

→ x = 12

The two numbers are:

5x = 5 × 12 = 60

8x = 8 × 12 = 96

The difference between the two numbers:

→ 96 - 60 = 36

**The difference between the two numbers is 36.**

questions.question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 196 and 7 respectively. If one of the numbers is 49, then find the other number.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Use the fundamental relation: **Other number = (LCM × HCF) ÷ Given number**

Other number = (196 × 7) ÷ 49

Other number = 1372 ÷ 49 = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**LCM** of two numbers = 196

**HCF** of two numbers = 7

One number (a) = 49

**Formula Used:**

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b': **a × b = LCM(a, b) × HCF(a, b)**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2a0a23bcb71ab82bc61d0b1825fcecb3e960fd7155ac931fab9d21e674028265.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 49 × Other number = 196 × 7

⇒ Other number = (196 × 7) ÷ 49

⇒ Other number = 196 ÷ (49 ÷ 7)

⇒ Other number = 196 ÷ 7

⇒ Other number = 28

**∴ The correct answer is 28.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Product of Two Numbers

The product of any two positive integers is always equal to the product of their **Least Common Multiple (LCM)** and **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**.

HCF and LCM Relation

The **HCF** of two or more numbers is always a factor of their **LCM**. In this case, 7 is a factor of 196 (196 ÷ 7 = 28).

Co-prime Numbers

If two numbers are **co-prime**, their HCF is 1 and their LCM is equal to the product of the two numbers.</p

questions.question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 114 and 19 respectively. If one of the numbers is 57, then find the other number.

questions.question: The HCF and the LCM of two numbers are 19 and 342, respectively. If one of the numbers is (9)/(2) times of the other, what is the larger number?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since one number is 9/2 times the other, their ratio is 2 : 9.

Because 2 and 9 are co-prime, their Highest Common Factor (HCF) corresponds exactly to 1 ratio unit.

Given the HCF is 19, we know that 1 ratio unit = 19.

The larger number corresponds to 9 ratio units.

Larger number = 9 × 19 = 171.

**∴ The correct answer is 171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

HCF = 19

LCM = 342

One number is 9/2 times the other. Let the smaller number be x, making the larger number (9/2)x.

**Formula Used:**

Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM

 Smaller Number Larger Number

• 2 units 9 units Ratio = 2 : 9 1 unit = HCF = 19 Larger Number = 9 × 19 = 171 

**Calculations:**

⇒ x × (9/2)x = 19 × 342

⇒ (9/2)x² = 19 × (19 × 18)

⇒ x² = 19 × 19 × 18 × (2/9)

⇒ x² = 19 × 19 × 4

⇒ x² = 1444

⇒ x = 38

⇒ Larger number = (9/2) × 38 = 171.

**∴ The correct answer is 171.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF and LCM Product Rule

For any two positive integers A and B, the product of their HCF and LCM is equal to the product of the numbers themselves. Formula: A × B = HCF × LCM.

Ratio and HCF Connection

If two numbers are in the ratio a : b (where a and b are co-prime), the numbers can be represented directly as (HCF × a) and (HCF × b).

LCM from Ratio and HCF

Using the co-prime ratio components a and b, the LCM can be found directly without the actual numbers using the formula: LCM = HCF × a × b.

questions.question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 192 and 32 respectively. If one of the numbers is 64, then find the other number.

questions.question: LCM and HCF of two numbers are 162 and 27 respectively. If one of the numbers is 54, then find the other number

**__Additional Information__**

Fundamental Property

For any two positive integers a and b, **LCM(a, b)** × **HCF(a, b)** = a × b.

HCF as a Factor

The **HCF** of two or more numbers is always a factor of their **LCM**.

Co-prime Numbers
